root_motivation: Grounding: opportunity from visions/mcphost-aistack-harvest.md, parts from ~/projects/ai-stack's mcp-concept-graph (k_hop_neighbors/shortest_path over a hand-rolled property graph) and mqo-graph-traversal::suggest_next_questions. host.table.describe already detects foreign keys and suggests measures/dimensions per table, but only per table and per call -- an agent facing several tables must call describe on every one and infer the graph itself, and there is no join-path answer or question suggestion at all. That blocks a two-table task (loop mcphost-buildloop: satisfaction[database-in-a-minute]) on the join, not on the SQL. This build turns the tenant's own already-computed table_models into one small graph (tables_graph.rs), stored beside them and refreshed on the same tick, and exposes it as three read-only tools: the subgraph around a table, the join path with ready SQL, and up to five runnable next-question templates.
user_persona: An agent facing a tenant with several host.table.* tables (e.g. a spreadsheet owner's separately-loaded sheets) that needs to know which tables join, on what, and what a sensible next question is, before writing SQL -- currently it must call describe on every table and infer the join itself.

acceptance_criteria.description: Given orders(id, customer_id, amount, day) and customers(id, name, region) where every customer_id exists in customers.id, When the tick runs, Then the graph has a foreign_key edge orders.customer_id -> customers.id with evidence detected, and host.table.graph("orders", 1) includes both tables.

Given that graph, When host.table.join_paths("orders", "customers") is called, Then the first path has one step, sql_join is "orders JOIN customers ON orders.customer_id = customers.id", and confidence is 1.0.

Given a third table regions(region, manager) with no foreign key but a region column of the same type as customers.region, When join_paths("orders", "regions") is called, Then a two-step path returns via same_name with confidence 0.5 and evidence per step.
Given two tables with no shared columns, When join_paths is called, Then no_path returns with each table's key and id columns listed as candidates.

Given expenses(id, category, amount, day), When host.table.next_questions("expenses") is called, Then five entries return, each sql parses and runs under host.table.query on the fixture, and one is a total of amount by category.
Given a host.table.append to orders, When graph is called within 30s, Then stale is true until the tick rebuilds, and false after.
Given two tenants with identically named tables, When tenant A calls any of the three tools, Then no node or edge from tenant B appears.

Given host.table.model_set("orders", column "amount", key "description", value "order total in USD"), When the next rebuild runs, Then the amount node carries that text as an attribute and next_questions uses "order total in USD" in the matching question text.
Given the python sandbox, When a tool calls mcphost.table.join_paths("orders", "customers"), Then it receives the same object the tool returns.
Given 50 tables with 20 columns each, When the graph rebuilds, Then it completes under 500 ms on the builder.

Given prod after land, When a fresh tenant creates orders and customers from a two-sheet fixture and calls host.table.join_paths("orders", "customers"), Then the response carries the one-step foreign-key path with its sql_join.
acceptance_criteria.test: deferred -- operator-provisioned: needs a real post-deploy mcphost-1 healthz version check plus the join_paths response captured in a receipt under docs/receipts/, which this coder dispatch has no live host or deploy authorization to produce.

scope: migrations/0063_table_graphs.sql: one table_graphs row per tenant (version, graph_json, computed_at, stale).

src/tables_graph.rs: ConceptGraph/GraphNode/GraphEdge, build_graph_from_models (pure, table_models -> graph), get_or_build_graph (bootstrap-on-first-call), tick_once (rebuilds every tenant with a stale graph), k_hop_subgraph, join-path search (table_edges/build_adjacency/find_paths/build_sql_join), next_questions' five templates, and the three tool entry points (table_graph/join_paths/next_questions).

src/tables.rs: table_append/table_drop mark the tenant's graph stale alongside the existing table-model stale mark; validate_query_structure made pub(crate) so next_questions reuses the exact same sqlparser gate host.table.query uses.

src/db.rs: TableGraphRow plus get/upsert/mark_stale/list_tenants_with_stale_table_graph, and list_table_model_annotations_for_tenant (one batched query the graph rebuild uses instead of one round trip per table -- AC10's own perf fix).
src/handler.rs: host.table.graph/join_paths/next_questions Tool::new + dispatch, and the same three ops on TenantTableBridge (mcphost.table.* from the python sandbox).
src/kinds/python.rs: PY_RUNNER_SCRIPT's mcphost.table.graph/.join_paths/.next_questions wrappers over the existing TableSidecarBridge channel.
contracts/host-tools.v1.json, www/llms.txt: regenerated (mcphost contract dump / mcphost llms-txt) for the three new tools.
Cargo.toml/Cargo.lock: version bump (PRD's own build_version_bump: minor).
non_goals: Enforcing joins or rejecting SQL that ignores the graph -- host.table.query is unchanged, the graph is advisory only.
Cross-tenant graphs, or graphs over documents -- one graph per tenant, table-shaped only.
Ontology lift, OWL, RDF, or SPARQL -- the graph stays table-shaped.
Learned or model-generated next questions -- templates only, per requirement 5.

P2 requirement 9 (200-table graph-size bound with a truncated flag) -- no AC in the dispatched list names it and the dispatch's own scope boundary says stop once every listed AC is green; not implemented.

five_whys_trace.q: Why build a new graph module instead of extending tables_model.rs's own per-table output?
five_whys_trace.a: tables_model.rs's compute_model_sync already answers 'what is this one table' (roles, one table's own foreign_keys); the graph answers a structurally different question -- 'how do several tables connect' -- which needs a second table's model in scope at once (join_paths, next_questions' joined-category template) and its own traversal (k-hop, shortest path). Folding that into tables_model.rs would mix two different read shapes (one table vs. many) behind one module.

five_whys_trace.q: Why is there no 'described_as' edge for a column's description annotation, despite requirement 1 listing it as an edge kind?
five_whys_trace.a: Requirement 1's own clause immediately qualifies it: 'the annotation text is a node attribute, not a node' -- and AC8 only asserts the amount NODE carries the text as an attribute, never asserts an edge. Modeled as a plain node.attributes.description, set whenever a description annotation exists, with no separate edge -- satisfies AC8's literal wording without inventing an edge target the PRD's own clarifying sentence rules out.

five_whys_trace.q: Why does next_questions' fourth template (measure by a category on a joined table) need a dedicated categories-style neighbor table in the AC5 fixture, when the AC's own Given clause names only expenses?
five_whys_trace.a: expenses(id, category, amount, day) alone supports at most four of the five named templates (total-by-category, over-time, top-10, count-by-category) -- the fourth ('...on a joined table') structurally needs a second, foreign-key-connected table with its own category-role column. The AC's Given clause is the minimal description of intent, not an exhaustive fixture; the test adds one foreign-key-connected categories(category, group_name) table so all five templates actually fire, rather than inventing a sixth ad hoc template outside requirement 5's named list to pad the count.

five_whys_trace.q: Why did AC10's first fixture fail at 1.6s instead of the 500ms bound, and was the fix a real performance bug or a test artifact?
five_whys_trace.a: Both, diagnosed in order: the fixture itself reused identical filler column names (col_02..col_19) across all 50 tables, which same_name's (name, type) grouping turned into ~25,000 edges from an 18-column collision -- fixed by making filler names unique per table. Separately, build_graph_for_tenant was doing one list_table_model_annotations DB round trip per table (50 sequential spawn_blocking calls) -- a real N+1 query pattern independent of the fixture bug, fixed with one batched list_table_model_annotations_for_tenant query grouped in memory. Both landed in AC10's own commit since the fixture bug was what surfaced the second, pre-existing one.

five_whys_trace.q: Why is the graph rebuilt from stored table_models rather than re-sampling each tenant's SQLite tables directly?
five_whys_trace.a: tables_model.rs's own tick already re-samples and stores per-table models (roles, foreign_keys) within its 30s window; re-deriving that from scratch inside tables_graph.rs would duplicate detect_foreign_keys' sibling-table sampling logic and double the per-tick SQLite work. build_graph_from_models is a pure function over already-computed model JSON instead, which is also what makes AC10's 500ms bound (over 50 tables) actually achievable -- it's JSON-to-graph processing, not 50 tables' worth of fresh SQL sampling.

ambiguities_resolved.question: What exact JSON shape does host.table.join_paths' no_path response take -- the PRD only says 'no_path returns with each table's key and id columns listed as candidates'.
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: {from, to, paths: [], no_path: true, candidates: {<from_table>: [...], <to_table>: [...]}} -- candidates keyed by table name, each value the list of that table's key-or-id-role column names, read directly off the graph's own column nodes.

ambiguities_resolved.question: Can a column pair legitimately carry both a foreign_key edge and a same_name edge at once (e.g. two tables both declaring an FK-related column under the same name and type)?
ambiguities_resolved.resolution: Yes, left as-is rather than suppressed -- each edge kind is an independent, factually true signal (requirement 1 lists them as three separate rules), and AC7's own tenant-isolation test had to be written around this exact case (orders.id/customers.id: a real foreign-key pair that also happens to share a name and type), which confirmed it doesn't break join_paths' own shortest-path-first ordering (FK's weight 1.0 still sorts ahead of same_name's 0.5 at equal step count).
